title: Formal glueing of a module map with I-power torsion kernel and cokernel
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a flat ring map of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] and $I\subseteq R$ a finitely generated ideal such that the induced map $R/I\to S/IS$ is an isomorphism. An $R$-module $T$ is *$I$-power torsion* if every $x\in T$ is killed by some power $I^e$; an $S$-module is $I$-power torsion if it is so as an $R$-module. For an $R$-module $P$ write $P\otimes_RS$ for the base change [def-weil-module-base-change] and $u\otimes_RS$ for the base change of an $R$-linear map $u$. (1) Given an $R$-module $N$, an $S$-module $M'$ and an $S$-linear map $\varphi':M'\to N\otimes_RS$ whose kernel and cokernel are $I$-power torsion, there exist an $R$-module $M$, an $R$-linear map $\psi:M\to N$ and an $S$-linear isomorphism $\beta:M'\to M\otimes_RS$ with $(\psi\otimes_RS)\circ\beta=\varphi'$. (2) Given an $R$-module $M$, an $S$-module $N'$ and an $S$-linear map $\varphi':M\otimes_RS\to N'$ whose kernel and cokernel are $I$-power torsion, there exist an $R$-module $N$, an $R$-linear map $\psi:M\to N$ and an $S$-linear isomorphism $\beta:N\otimes_RS\to N'$ with $\beta\circ(\psi\otimes_RS)=\varphi'$. (3) In both cases $\operatorname{Ker}\psi$ and $\operatorname{Coker}\psi$ are $I$-power torsion, and the canonical maps $\operatorname{Ker}\psi\to\operatorname{Ker}(\psi\otimes_RS)$, $\operatorname{Coker}\psi\to\operatorname{Coker}(\psi\otimes_RS)$ induced by $x\mapsto x\otimes1$ are isomorphisms of $R$-modules; hence, via $\beta$, $\operatorname{Ker}\psi\cong\operatorname{Ker}\varphi'$ and $\operatorname{Coker}\psi\cong\operatorname{Coker}\varphi'$.

proof.text: For any $I$-power torsion module $A$, replace an annihilating exponent $n$ by $n+1$ using $I^{n+1}\subseteq I^n$. Convert the bijective quotient map into a ring equivalence. Apply torsion base change, identify the restricted scalar action with the algebra action, and compose with tensor symmetry. This gives an $R$-linear equivalence $A\to S\otimes_R A$ whose value on $a$ is $1\otimes a$.

proof.text: Flatness gives Mathlib LinearMap.tensorKerEquiv, whose pure-tensor formula identifies $S\otimes_R\ker\psi$ with the base-changed kernel. Compose it with the preceding torsion equivalence. For the cokernel, use TensorProduct.tensorQuotientEquiv. LinearMap.lTensor_range equates the tensor image of the range subtype with the range of the tensor map; Submodule.quotEquivOfEq therefore identifies its target with the desired cokernel. Compose with the torsion equivalence of the cokernel. On representatives both constructions send $x$ to $1\otimes x$.

proof.text: In the map-to case, restrict $\beta^{-1}$ to the base-changed kernel, with inverse the restriction of $\beta$. The factorization proves membership on both sides. The ranges are equal because $\beta$ is surjective; compose the cokernel comparison with the quotient equivalence of that equality. In the map-from case, the factorization and injectivity of $\beta$ identify the two kernels by the identity map. The factorization also proves that $\beta$ maps the base-changed range onto the original range; Submodule.Quotient.equiv induces the cokernel equivalence. The pure-tensor formulas and the inverse laws of $\beta$ give exactly the last two requested clauses.
